/tours/grand-egyptian-museum-pyramids-to.name: Grand Egyptian Museum & Pyramids Tour In Cairo

sections.h: Why See the Grand Egyptian Museum and the Pyramids Together
body: The Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) stands on the edge of the Giza plateau, about two kilometers from the pyramids, so both visits fit into one day with very little time lost in Cairo traffic. Starting at the museum gives the pyramids their context: by the time you reach the plateau you have already seen the statues, tools and burial treasures of the people who built them, and your Egyptologist guide can link what you saw indoors to the monuments outside.

The museum opened fully to visitors in November 2025 and is the largest museum in the world devoted to a single civilization. It is huge, so a guide who knows the layout makes a real difference: instead of wandering, you follow a route through the galleries that interest you most and still have energy left for the afternoon.
**The Grand Hall:** the colossal red-granite statue of Ramses II, which stood in Cairo's Ramses Square for half a century, now welcomes visitors at the entrance.
**The Grand Staircase:** a monumental staircase lined with statues of kings and gods, rising to a window with a view of the pyramids.
**The Tutankhamun galleries:** the complete contents of the boy king's tomb, found by Howard Carter in 1922, displayed together for the first time — more than 5,000 objects.
**The Khufu boat:** a 4,500-year-old cedar boat discovered beside the Great Pyramid, now shown in its own hall.
**The main galleries:** thousands of objects arranged by theme and era, from prehistoric Egypt to the Greek and Roman period.

sections.h: The Giza Pyramids and the Great Sphinx
body: After an optional lunch break, the tour continues to the Giza plateau. The Great Pyramid of Khufu, built around 2560 BC, is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing. Beside it rise the pyramids of his son Khafre — which looks taller only because it stands on higher ground — and of Menkaure, the smallest of the three. Your guide explains how they were built and what they meant to the kings buried inside. The day ends at the Great Sphinx, carved from the bedrock of the plateau, with time for photographs from the best viewpoints.
Wear comfortable shoes: expect around two hours of walking inside the museum and about the same on the plateau.
Bring sunglasses, a hat and sunscreen. There is little shade around the pyramids, even in winter.
Camel and horse rides at the pyramids are optional and not included. If you would like one, ask your guide to help you agree on the price before you ride.
Pickup and drop-off are included from any hotel in Cairo or Giza, and the tour is private, so the pace follows your group.

sections.h: Make More of Your Time in Cairo
body: With one more day, add the [Saqqara, Memphis and Dahshur day trip](/tours/saqqara-memphis-dahshur-day-trip-from-cairo/) to see where pyramid building began, or spend an evening on a [Nile dinner cruise](/tours/cairo-dinner-nile-cruise/). If you have already visited the GEM, the [Giza Pyramids and Saqqara tour](/tours/giza-pyramids-saqqara-tour/) pairs the plateau with the Step Pyramid instead. For the rest of the city — the Citadel, Khan El Khalili and Islamic Cairo — read our [Cairo travel guide](/blog/cairo-travel-guide-pyramids-museums-bazaars/).

sections.h: Why Fly Over Luxor at Sunrise
body: Luxor is one of the few places in the world where a balloon flight passes over 3,000-year-old temples and royal tombs. Flights leave the West Bank at dawn, when the air is cool and calm, so you rise into the sky just as the sun comes up over the Nile and the desert hills turn from gray to gold.

From above, the layout of ancient Thebes finally makes sense: the green strip of farmland along the river, where people lived and worked, and the dry cliffs beyond it, where the pharaohs chose to be buried. No ground tour gives you this view, and many travelers remember it as the highlight of their trip to Egypt.

sections.h: What You Can See From the Basket
body: **Valley of the Kings:** the desert valley where New Kingdom pharaohs, Tutankhamun among them, were buried in rock-cut tombs.
**Temple of Hatshepsut:** the terraced temple of Egypt's best-known female pharaoh, set against the cliffs of Deir el-Bahari.
**Colossi of Memnon:** two giant seated statues of Amenhotep III that have stood on the West Bank for about 3,400 years.
**The Nile and the West Bank villages:** sugar-cane fields, palm groves and mud-brick houses, with the city of Luxor across the river.
The exact flight path depends on the wind that morning, so the pilot cannot promise to pass over a particular monument — but the whole West Bank is spread out below you.

sections.h: Shared Basket or VIP Private Basket
body: The standard option is a shared balloon. Shared baskets are large and divided into compartments, so every passenger stands at the edge with a clear view. For a honeymoon, an anniversary or a proposal, the VIP private basket keeps the balloon for your group alone; its price depends on the date and the number of people, so send us a request and we will quote it. Both options include hotel pickup, the Nile crossing, the safety briefing and your flight certificate.

sections.h: Weather, Safety and What to Wear
body: Balloon flights in Luxor are licensed and supervised by the Egyptian Civil Aviation Authority, and every flight is flown by a certified pilot. Each morning the wind is checked before take-off is allowed. If flights are cancelled because of the weather, which happens on some mornings, we help you rebook another day during your stay or arrange a refund under our [refund policy](/refund_returns-2/).
Dress in layers: desert mornings can be cold before sunrise, especially from November to February, and warm up quickly afterwards.
Wear flat, closed shoes to climb in and out of the basket safely.
Keep your phone or camera on a strap — you will want photos from take-off to landing. Our [Egypt photography tips](/blog/egypt-photography-tips-travel-camera-gear/) help you get them right.
Tell us in advance about pregnancy, young children, or back or heart conditions, so we can check with the operator before you book.
At landing, follow the pilot's instructions and take the landing position you practiced in the briefing.

sections.h: Make the Most of Your Morning in Luxor
body: The flight is over by breakfast time, so it combines easily with sightseeing the same day — many guests go straight on to the West Bank monuments they have just seen from the air. On a Nile cruise, the balloon is an optional extra on the Luxor day of our [4-day cruise from Aswan to Luxor](/nile-cruises/4-days-nile-cruise-aswan-to-luxor/). Staying on the Red Sea? A dawn flight needs a night in Luxor, so ask us to add an overnight stay to the [Luxor day trip from Hurghada](/tours/luxor-day-trip-from-hurghada/). Our [Luxor travel guide](/blog/luxor-egypt-travel-guide-temples-balloon/) has more ideas for your visit.

Ramses II had the two temples of Abu Simbel cut into a sandstone cliff above the Nile in the 13th century BC, near the southern edge of his empire. The Great Temple honors the gods Amun, Ra-Horakhty and Ptah — and Ramses himself — behind four seated statues of the king, each about 20 meters tall. The smaller temple is dedicated to the goddess Hathor and to Nefertari, his favorite queen, and it is one of the few temples in Egypt where a queen's statues stand as tall as the king's.

In the 1960s, the building of the Aswan High Dam threatened to drown both temples under Lake Nasser. In one of the greatest rescue projects in the history of archaeology, an international campaign led by UNESCO cut the temples into more than a thousand blocks and rebuilt them on higher ground between 1964 and 1968. Today they are part of the Nubian Monuments UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The Great Temple was aligned so that twice a year, around 22 February and 22 October, the first rays of the rising sun travel deep inside and light up the statues in the inner sanctuary. Only the statue of Ptah, a god often linked with the underworld, stays in shadow. Thousands of visitors come for these mornings, so if you want to see the Sun Festival, contact us early and we will plan a very early departure from Aswan.

sections.h: Planning Your Day Trip From Aswan
body: **Timing:** private tours usually leave Aswan at around 4:00 am, so you reach the temples before the midday heat and the biggest crowds. Because the tour is private, the departure time can be adjusted.
**The drive:** about 280 km each way, or three to three and a half hours through the desert, on a well-maintained road with tourist police checkpoints.
**Private car or minivan:** a private car suits couples and small families, while the private minivan gives larger groups more space at a lower price per person.
**Food:** lunch is not included, but you can add a lunch box when booking. Bring snacks and water for the road.
**At the temples:** guides explain the history outside, then you explore the interiors at your own pace. Allow about two hours on site.
**What to bring:** a hat, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable shoes — the site is open and sunny, with a short walk from the entrance along the shore of Lake Nasser.

sections.h: Combine Abu Simbel With Your Nile Trip
body: Abu Simbel is usually visited from Aswan, either as a day trip before or after a Nile cruise or as part of a longer holiday. Our [3-night cruise from Aswan](/nile-cruises/3-nights-nile-cruise-from-aswan-including-abu-simbel/) and [4-night cruise from Luxor](/nile-cruises/4-nights-nile-cruise-from-luxor-including-abu-simbel/) both include the visit, and the [8-day Cairo, Abu Simbel, Luxor and Hurghada package](/packages/8-days-cairo-abu-simbel-luxor-hurghada/) builds it into a full holiday. For more time in the south, read our [Aswan guide](/blog/aswan-egypt-guide-temples-nubian-villages-sunsets/) and our tips for [visiting a Nubian village](/blog/nubian-village-tour-aswan-nightlife-music-hospitality/).

sections.h: Two Chapters of the Pyramid Story in One Day
body: This tour visits the two sites that best tell the story of the pyramids. At Saqqara you see where it began: the Step Pyramid of King Djoser, designed by his architect Imhotep around 2670 BC as a stack of six stone steps. At Giza you see where it peaked, roughly a century later, with the smooth-sided pyramids of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure. Visiting both on the same day, with an Egyptologist explaining what changed in between, turns a list of famous monuments into one story.

sections.h: What You Will See at Giza
body: **The Great Pyramid of Khufu:** built from an estimated 2.3 million stone blocks and originally about 146 meters tall, it remained the tallest human-made structure on Earth for more than 3,800 years.
**The Pyramid of Khafre:** it looks taller than the Great Pyramid because it stands on higher ground, and it still keeps some of its original smooth casing stones near the top.
**The Pyramid of Menkaure:** the smallest of the three main pyramids, with the small pyramids of its queens beside it.

**The Great Sphinx and the Valley Temple:** the lion with a king's head, carved from the bedrock of the plateau, and the granite temple beside it where the funeral rites of King Khafre are thought to have begun.
**The panoramic viewpoint:** the classic photo spot where all the pyramids line up against the desert.

Saqqara lies less than an hour's drive south of Giza and served as the burial ground of Memphis, Egypt's first capital, for about 3,000 years. The Step Pyramid is the oldest pyramid in Egypt, and the complex around it — with its entrance colonnade and ceremonial courtyards — shows how Egypt's architects first learned to build in stone. Saqqara is far quieter than Giza, so you have time to take in the site with your guide and take photographs without the crowds.

sections.h: Good to Know Before You Go
body: Start early if you can: the plateau is cooler and less crowded in the morning.
Going inside one of the pyramids needs its own ticket. The passages are steep, narrow and warm, so skip it if you dislike tight spaces.
Camel and horse rides at Giza are optional and not included. Your guide can help you choose a reliable ride and agree on the price first.
Wear comfortable shoes and bring a hat, sunscreen and sunglasses. Bottled water is provided during the tour.
The optional lunch stop is at a local restaurant serving Egyptian dishes — a good chance to try the [local food](/blog/egyptian-food-guide-authentic-flavors/).

To go deeper into the pyramid story, the [Saqqara, Memphis and Dahshur day trip](/tours/saqqara-memphis-dahshur-day-trip-from-cairo/) adds the Bent and Red Pyramids and the ancient capital, Memphis. For the treasures found inside the tombs, book the [Grand Egyptian Museum and Pyramids tour](/tours/grand-egyptian-museum-pyramids-tour/), and end a day of sightseeing with a [Nile dinner cruise](/tours/cairo-dinner-nile-cruise/). Our [Cairo travel guide](/blog/cairo-travel-guide-pyramids-museums-bazaars/) covers the rest of the city.

/tours/luxor-day-trip-from-hurghada/.name: Luxor Day Trip From Hurghada Private Tour

sections.h: Is a Day Trip From Hurghada to Luxor Worth It?
body: Yes, if you are based on the Red Sea and have only one day for ancient Egypt. Luxor, the ancient city of Thebes, was the religious capital of Egypt for much of the New Kingdom, and it holds more great monuments than almost anywhere else in the country. It is a long day — about four hours' drive each way — but a private car, an Egyptologist guide and a well-planned route mean you see the major sites of both the East and West Banks and still sleep in your own hotel that night.

The trip suits guests staying in Hurghada, Makadi Bay, El Gouna, Soma Bay and Safaga, and the private format lets you set the pace, spend longer at the sites you enjoy most and stop whenever you need to.
**Karnak Temple:** a vast complex built and expanded over some 2,000 years. Its Great Hypostyle Hall holds 134 giant columns, many still covered in carvings and traces of their original paint.

**Valley of the Kings:** the royal burial ground of the New Kingdom, where more than 60 tombs have been found. Your ticket covers several of the open tombs, with their painted walls and ceilings; Tutankhamun's tomb needs an extra ticket.
**Temple of Hatshepsut:** the terraced temple of Egypt's most famous female pharaoh, built against the cliffs of Deir el-Bahari.
**Colossi of Memnon:** a photo stop at the two giant statues of Amenhotep III on the West Bank.
**Lunch in Luxor:** a meal at a local restaurant is included before you cross to the West Bank.

Pickup is early in the morning, usually before sunrise, so that you reach Luxor while the temples are still cool. The road from the coast crosses the Eastern Desert via Safaga and Qena, with rest stops along the way and regular police checkpoints. You visit the East Bank first, have lunch, then cross the Nile to the West Bank before starting the drive home in the late afternoon. Expect to be back at your hotel in the evening, 14 to 16 hours after you left.

sections.h: Tips for a Long Day Out
body: Go to bed early the night before and use the drive to rest; the car is air-conditioned and bottled water is provided.
Bring a hat, sunglasses and sunscreen. Luxor is much hotter and drier than the coast, especially from May to September.
Wear comfortable shoes: there is plenty of walking at Karnak and in the Valley of the Kings.
Carry some Egyptian pounds for tips, drinks and optional extras such as the Tutankhamun tomb ticket.

If one day feels too rushed, ask us to add a night in Luxor. You could then take the sunrise [Luxor hot air balloon](/tours/luxor-hot-air-balloon/) flight the next morning and see more of the West Bank. For the full picture of ancient Egypt, a [4-day Nile cruise from Aswan to Luxor](/nile-cruises/4-days-nile-cruise-aswan-to-luxor/) covers the temples of the Nile Valley at a slower pace. Planning the rest of your Red Sea stay? Try the [Orange Bay snorkeling trip](/tours/orange-bay-island-snorkeling/) and read our [Hurghada vs Sharm El Sheikh guide](/blog/red-sea-egypt-resorts-hurghada-vs-sharm-guide/).

/tours/saqqara-memphis-dahshur-day-trip-.name: Saqqara, Memphis & Dahshur Day Trip from Cairo

body: Most visitors to Cairo see Giza and leave. This tour shows what came before it. In roughly a century, Egypt's builders went from a stepped pyramid at Saqqara to the first true, smooth-sided pyramid at Dahshur, and every stop on this route is a step in that experiment. With your guide explaining each site in order, you finish the day understanding why the Great Pyramid looks the way it does.
The three sites lie close together south of Giza and are far quieter than the Giza plateau, so you can explore at an easy pace and take photographs without the crowds.

sections.h: Saqqara: The Step Pyramid of Djoser
body: Around 2670 BC, the architect Imhotep built a tomb for King Djoser by stacking six stone platforms on top of one another. The result, the Step Pyramid, is the oldest pyramid in Egypt and one of the earliest large stone buildings in the world. It stands inside a walled complex with a grand entrance colonnade and courtyards used for royal ceremonies. Saqqara remained the burial ground of Memphis for about 3,000 years, and new discoveries are still announced there almost every year.

According to tradition, King Menes founded Memphis around 3100 BC when he united Upper and Lower Egypt, and it remained one of the country's most important cities for thousands of years. Little of the ancient city survives above ground today, but the open-air museum at Mit Rahina keeps two of its treasures: a colossal limestone statue of Ramses II, now lying on its back so you can see the fine detail of his face, and the Alabaster Sphinx, the largest calcite statue ever found in Egypt.

sections.h: Dahshur: The Bent and Red Pyramids
body: At Dahshur, King Sneferu, the father of Khufu, tried twice to build a true pyramid. The Bent Pyramid changes angle halfway up, most likely because the builders realized the original slope was too steep to be stable. The Red Pyramid, named for the reddish tone of its stone, got it right: it is the first successful smooth-sided pyramid and the model for the Great Pyramid at Giza. When it is open, you can climb down a long, low passage into its burial chambers — a memorable experience if you are comfortable in tight spaces.
Entrance tickets for the three sites are paid separately. Bring a bank card as well as some cash, and your guide will help at each ticket office.
Wear comfortable shoes and a hat; the sites are open and sunny. Bottled water is provided during the tour.
Lunch is optional — add it when booking and the tour stops at a local restaurant on the way back.
Allow six to eight hours in total, including pickup and drop-off at your hotel in Cairo or Giza.
Photography is welcome outdoors at all three sites, and Dahshur's open desert setting is especially photogenic.
You will be back at your hotel with time to rest before an evening [Nile dinner cruise](/tours/cairo-dinner-nile-cruise/), a relaxing way to end the day.

sections.h: Pair It With Giza and the GEM
body: This trip works best alongside a day at Giza. See the finished masterpieces on the [Giza Pyramids and Saqqara tour](/tours/giza-pyramids-saqqara-tour/) or the [Grand Egyptian Museum and Pyramids tour](/tours/grand-egyptian-museum-pyramids-tour/), where many objects from these same sites are on display. Our [Cairo travel guide](/blog/cairo-travel-guide-pyramids-museums-bazaars/) helps you plan the rest of your stay.

sections.h: Why Orange Bay Is Hurghada's Favorite Island Trip
body: Orange Bay sits on Giftun Island, a short boat ride from Hurghada Marina, inside the protected Giftun Islands area of the Red Sea. It is known for its soft white sand, shallow turquoise lagoon and clear water, which is why it appears in so many photos of Hurghada. Because the sea around the island is calm and shallow, it is one of the easiest places on the coast to try snorkeling for the first time.

The day combines a relaxing cruise, a snorkeling stop over coral reefs and free time on the beach, with lunch and soft drinks served on board. There is no rush and nothing to organize: hotel pickup, the boat, the equipment and your meal are all arranged for you.
The Red Sea is one of the world's great snorkeling destinations, home to more than 1,000 species of fish and warm water all year.
Colorful parrotfish, butterflyfish and angelfish around the coral heads
Clownfish living among sea anemones
Hard and soft corals in shallow water, easy to see from the surface
With luck, a sea turtle or a pod of dolphins along the way
Sightings are never guaranteed, but even beginners floating near the boat see plenty of marine life.

Orange Bay is a good choice for families, couples and groups of friends with mixed experience in the water. No snorkeling experience is needed: the crew provides snorkeling equipment and life jackets, and non-swimmers can stay in the shallows or relax on the beach. Children aged 5 to 11 pay the child price, and infants usually join free of charge.

After hotel pickup, a short cruise from Hurghada Marina brings you to the reefs around Giftun Island. The crew chooses the snorkeling spot on the day, depending on the wind and the sea, and gives everyone a quick briefing before you get in the water. Afterwards you head to Orange Bay for a few relaxed hours of swimming and sunbathing, with lunch served on board before the cruise back to the marina in the afternoon.

sections.h: Tips for a Great Day at Sea
body: Bring a swimsuit, a towel, sunglasses, a hat and a change of clothes.
Use reef-safe sunscreen and put it on before boarding. The sun is strong on the water even when the breeze feels cool.
Never touch or stand on the coral, and do not feed the fish; the reefs are protected and very fragile.
If you get seasick, take a tablet before the boat leaves and stay on the open deck.
Bring an underwater camera or a waterproof phone case for the reef.
Leave valuables at your hotel and bring a small waterproof bag for your phone and cash.
Pickup is usually around 8:00 am, and we confirm the exact time the day before.

The trip runs all year. From about May to October the sea is at its warmest, while winter days are milder and sometimes windier, with the water typically in the low 20s °C — still pleasant for most swimmers.

sections.h: More to Do on the Red Sea
body: Staying longer in Hurghada? Take a [Luxor day trip from Hurghada](/tours/luxor-day-trip-from-hurghada/) to see Karnak and the Valley of the Kings, or build your beach time into the [7-day Cairo and Hurghada holiday](/packages/7-days-cairo-hurghada-holiday/). Heading to Sharm El Sheikh instead? The [Ras Mohammed snorkeling trip](/tours/ras-mohammed-snorkeling/) visits one of the Red Sea's most famous marine parks. Compare the two resorts in our [Hurghada vs Sharm El Sheikh guide](/blog/red-sea-egypt-resorts-hurghada-vs-sharm-guide/), and check our [Egypt packing list](/blog/egypt-packing-list-essential-items/) before you go.

/tours/cairo-dinner-nile-cruise/.name: Luxury Cairo Dinner Nile Cruise With Entertainment Show

sections.h: An Evening on the Nile in the Heart of Cairo
body: After a day of pyramids and museums, the Nile is the best place to see Cairo at its most relaxed. On this dinner cruise you board a floating restaurant in central Cairo and sail slowly along the river while the city lights up around you: the illuminated bridges, the Cairo Tower on Gezira Island and the hotels along the Corniche. Dinner, music and live shows fill the evening, and hotel pickup and drop-off are included, so there is nothing to arrange.
It is one of the most popular evening activities in Cairo, and a good way to spend your first or last night in Egypt.

Your driver collects you from your hotel in Cairo or Giza in the early evening and takes you to the marina, where the crew welcomes you on board and shows you to your table. Dinner is served soon after the boat casts off, and the shows follow while you sail. The boat moves slowly through central Cairo for around two hours, so there is time to eat, watch the performers and step out on deck for photographs of the city lights before returning to the dock and your ride back to the hotel.
**Tanoura show:** a traditional Egyptian dance with roots in Sufi whirling. The dancer spins for many minutes without stopping, and the layered, brightly colored skirts open out like wheels of color.
**Belly dance:** a performance of raqs sharqi, the classic Egyptian style of belly dancing, set to Egyptian music.
**Live entertainment:** music and shows through the evening, which vary by boat and by night.

Dinner is an open buffet of Egyptian and international dishes, typically with grilled meats, rice, vegetables, salads, bread and desserts. It is a relaxed way to try Egyptian favorites alongside familiar options. Drinks are not included in the price and can be ordered on board. If you are vegetarian or have allergies or other dietary needs, tell us in the special requests field when you book.

The cruise offers standard and VIP seats. VIP seating usually means a better-placed table, closer to the shows and the river views. Prices change with the boat, the date and your seating choice, so send us a request with your date and number of guests and we will reply with the best option available.

The cruise suits honeymooners, families with children and groups of friends, and it is an easy choice for solo travelers who want a safe, organized evening out. It also works well if you prefer a relaxed evening at a table to a walking tour; some boats have stairs, so let us know if you need help boarding.
The whole evening, including transfers, takes about three to four hours.
Smart-casual clothes are ideal for the evening.
In winter, bring a light jacket if you want to step out on deck.
Children are welcome, and the evening is popular with families.
Choose a window table or step out on deck to photograph the city lights; a phone in night mode works well.
Celebrating a birthday or anniversary? Mention it when you book and we will let the crew know.
In the busy season, book a day or two ahead to secure your preferred seating.

sections.h: Plan the Rest of Your Cairo Stay
body: The dinner cruise fits neatly at the end of a sightseeing day, such as the [Giza Pyramids and Saqqara tour](/tours/giza-pyramids-saqqara-tour/) or the [Grand Egyptian Museum and Pyramids tour](/tours/grand-egyptian-museum-pyramids-tour/). It is also included on the first evening of our [7-day Cairo and Hurghada holiday](/packages/7-days-cairo-hurghada-holiday/). For restaurants, markets and more ideas, see our [Cairo travel guide](/blog/cairo-travel-guide-pyramids-museums-bazaars/) and [Egyptian food guide](/blog/egyptian-food-guide-authentic-flavors/).

/packages/total-solar-eclipse-tour-2027/.name: 2027 Total Solar Eclipse Tour: Nile Cruise & Luxor

sections.h: Why Watch the 2027 Eclipse From Luxor
body: On Monday 2 August 2027, the Moon will pass directly in front of the Sun and turn day into night along a narrow path across North Africa and the Middle East. Luxor lies close to the point of greatest eclipse, where totality lasts about 6 minutes 23 seconds — one of the longest total solar eclipses of the 21st century. Most total eclipses last less than four minutes.

Weather matters as much as location, and here Luxor is hard to beat: August skies over Upper Egypt are almost always clear, giving some of the best viewing odds anywhere on the eclipse path. The eclipse also happens around midday, with the Sun high in the sky above the Nile.

The trip is built around the eclipse date. You arrive in Aswan on Friday 30 July 2027, visit the High Dam, Philae Temple and the Unfinished Obelisk, take a felucca ride and board the 5-star Sonesta Nile Goddess. The next days are spent sailing north on a full-board basis, with guided visits along the way depending on the final sailing schedule. On Monday 2 August you are taken to a prime viewing location in Luxor for the eclipse itself. Transfers between the cruise and the airports of Aswan and Luxor, entrance fees in Aswan and Luxor, and the support of our team throughout are included.

**The partial phases:** the Moon takes more than an hour to cover the Sun, and about as long to uncover it. Wear certified eclipse glasses (ISO 12312-2) whenever you look at the Sun during these phases.

**Totality:** for just over six minutes the sky darkens, the air cools, bright planets and stars appear and the Sun's glowing corona comes into view. Only during totality is it safe to look without glasses.
**Cameras and binoculars:** never point them at the partly eclipsed Sun without a proper solar filter on the front of the lens.
**The moments before totality:** watch for faint shadow bands rippling across the ground and the ‘diamond ring’ as the last bead of sunlight disappears behind the Moon.
**No logistics to worry about:** our team takes you to the viewing location, so you can concentrate on the sky.

sections.h: Preparing for August in Upper Egypt
body: Expect daytime temperatures often above 40°C. Wear light, loose clothing, a wide-brimmed hat and sunscreen, and drink water all day.
Do your sightseeing early or late in the day where you can, and rest on the air-conditioned ship during the afternoon heat.
Bring your own certified eclipse glasses, plus a spare pair in case one gets lost or damaged.
Plan your onward flight for after the eclipse: the tour ends in Luxor on 2 August, and you will not want to miss totality for a check-in queue.
Keep your kit simple on the day: a hat, water, eclipse glasses and your camera are all you need at the viewing site.

Luxor will be one of the main destinations for eclipse travelers, and hotel rooms and Nile cruise cabins are expected to sell out well before the date. The prices in the table above are fixed per person for the whole trip, and your cabin is secured once your booking is confirmed. Send us your details through the booking form or on WhatsApp to reserve your place.

Want more time before or after the eclipse? Add Abu Simbel from Aswan with our [private day tour](/tours/abu-simbel-temples-private-tour/), or stay on in Luxor and see the West Bank from the air on a [sunrise balloon flight](/tours/luxor-hot-air-balloon/). Our [Luxor travel guide](/blog/luxor-egypt-travel-guide-temples-balloon/) and [Aswan guide](/blog/aswan-egypt-guide-temples-nubian-villages-sunsets/) will help you plan extra days.

/nile-cruises/4-days-nile-cruise-aswan-t.name: 4 Days Nile Cruise Aswan To Luxor

sections.h: Why Sail From Aswan to Luxor
body: The Nile flows north, so a cruise from Aswan to Luxor sails with the current. That makes this the shorter version of the classic route: three nights instead of four, visiting the same key temples as the longer cruise from Luxor. It suits travelers who want the full Nile experience without giving it a whole week, and it is easy to combine with a few days in Cairo or on the Red Sea.

Life on board is part of the appeal. Between visits you can relax on the sun deck, watch fishermen, villages and palm groves drift past, and enjoy all your meals on board on a full-board basis. The galabeya party on the second evening, when guests dress up in traditional Egyptian robes, is a fun highlight.
**Philae Temple:** the island temple of the goddess Isis, moved stone by stone to Agilkia Island in a UNESCO rescue project completed in 1980.
**The Unfinished Obelisk:** still lying in its ancient granite quarry, it would have been the largest obelisk ever raised had it not cracked during carving.
**The High Dam:** completed in 1970, it created Lake Nasser and changed life along the Nile for good.
**Kom Ombo:** a rare double temple, with one half for the crocodile god Sobek and the other for Horus the Elder. A small museum next to it displays mummified crocodiles.
**Edfu:** the Temple of Horus, completed in the Ptolemaic period and the best-preserved temple in Egypt, with its roof, walls and towering gateway still intact.
**Luxor:** the Valley of the Kings, the Temple of Hatshepsut and the Colossi of Memnon on the West Bank, then the vast temples of Karnak and Luxor on the East Bank.

Between Edfu and Luxor, the ship passes through the lock at Esna, where boats wait their turn to move between two levels of the river. Watching the huge gates open and close from the deck is an unexpected highlight for many passengers, and local traders often row up alongside the ships to sell tablecloths and galabeyas.
**Best time to go:** October to April brings pleasant temperatures for sightseeing; summer is hot but quieter, and often better value.
**Entrance fees:** they are not included in the base price — add them when you book and your guide handles the tickets at every site.
**Abu Simbel:** add a day trip from Aswan before you embark, or choose our [3-night cruise from Aswan including Abu Simbel](/nile-cruises/3-nights-nile-cruise-from-aswan-including-abu-simbel/).
**Sunrise balloon:** book the optional [Luxor hot air balloon](/tours/luxor-hot-air-balloon/) for the morning of day 3.
**Staying connected:** Wi-Fi on board is often limited, so a local SIM card is useful — see our [Egypt SIM card guide](/blog/egypt-sim-card-tourist-guide-nile-cruise/).
**Packing:** bring light layers — winter evenings on deck can be cool, while days at the temples are warm and sunny.

sections.h: Prefer a Longer or Slower Cruise?
body: If you have an extra day, the [5-day cruise from Luxor to Aswan](/nile-cruises/5-days-nile-river-cruise-from-luxor-to-aswan/) sails the same route upstream with more time on board. For a smaller, more intimate boat, look at our [4-day dahabiya cruise](/nile-cruises/4-days-dahabiya-nile-cruise-from-aswan-to-luxor/), and read why travelers love [slow travel on the Nile](/blog/nile-cruise-egypt-slow-travel-aswan-to-luxor/).

/nile-cruises/5-days-nile-river-cruise-f.name: 5 Days Nile River Cruise from Luxor to Aswan

sections.h: The Classic Nile Cruise, at an Easy Pace
body: Sailing from Luxor to Aswan means sailing upstream, against the current, so this route takes four nights instead of three. The extra time is spent on the water: long, quiet hours on the sun deck watching the Nile Valley go by, between guided visits to the greatest temples of Upper Egypt. It is the best choice if you want the cruise itself to be part of the holiday, not just a way of getting between sites.

Departures run on Saturdays and Mondays, and the package covers four nights on a 5-star cruise ship with full board, excursions with an Egyptologist guide, and entrance fees to all the sights between Luxor and Aswan.

sections.h: Luxor: Two Days in Ancient Thebes
body: The cruise starts where ancient Egypt's greatest temples stand. On day one you visit Karnak, a complex built and expanded over some 2,000 years, then return in the evening to see Luxor Temple lit up at night. The two temples were once linked by the Avenue of Sphinxes, a processional road nearly three kilometers long that has been restored and reopened. On day two you cross to the West Bank for the royal tombs of the Valley of the Kings, the terraced Temple of Hatshepsut and the Colossi of Memnon.
**The Esna lock:** on the way south the ship passes through the lock at Esna — a fun moment to watch from the deck.
**Edfu:** the Temple of Horus, the best-preserved temple in Egypt, with its roof and massive gateway still standing.
**Kom Ombo:** a double temple shared by the crocodile god Sobek and Horus the Elder, set right on the riverbank.
**Aswan:** the High Dam and Lake Nasser, the Unfinished Obelisk in its granite quarry, and Philae Temple, the island sanctuary of Isis, reached by motorboat.
**A felucca in Aswan:** on your last evening, an optional sunset sail on a traditional felucca around Elephantine Island is a lovely way to end the trip.

Cruise prices depend on the season and on how many people travel together. The lowest price is for groups of 9 to 16 travelers between May and September; couples and small groups of 2 to 4 pay more per person, and solo travelers pay the single price. Autumn, winter and the Christmas–New Year period are the busiest seasons and cost more. Every season and group size is listed in the price table above, or send us your dates for an exact quote. The price covers the cruise, meals on board, excursions and entrance fees, so the main extras to budget for are drinks, tips and any optional activities.
Light, breathable clothes for the day, and a warm layer for evenings on deck from November to February.
A hat, sunglasses and sunscreen for the open temple sites.
Comfortable walking shoes, plus swimwear for the sun deck.
Some small notes in Egyptian pounds for tips, which are not included.
For the full list, see our [Egypt packing list](/blog/egypt-packing-list-essential-items/).

The cruise ends in Aswan, which makes it easy to add Abu Simbel afterwards on our [private day tour](/tours/abu-simbel-temples-private-tour/). If you want Abu Simbel included in the cruise, choose the [4-night cruise from Luxor including Abu Simbel](/nile-cruises/4-nights-nile-cruise-from-luxor-including-abu-simbel/). Short on time? The [4-day cruise from Aswan to Luxor](/nile-cruises/4-days-nile-cruise-aswan-to-luxor/) covers the same temples in three nights. In Luxor, book a sunrise [hot air balloon flight](/tours/luxor-hot-air-balloon/) before you board, and in Aswan, spend an evening in a [Nubian village](/blog/nubian-village-tour-aswan-nightlife-music-hospitality/).

sections.h: The Best of Both Worlds in One Week
body: This holiday is built for travelers who want to see ancient Egypt and still have time to relax. The first three days are spent in Cairo, with the pyramids, the Grand Egyptian Museum and the historic heart of the city. Then a short domestic flight takes you to Hurghada for three nights on the Red Sea, with a snorkeling trip, a desert quad-bike safari and time on the beach. Flying instead of driving saves you a road trip of five to six hours each way.

Your first evening starts on the water with a Nile dinner cruise, complete with a belly dance performance and a Tanoura show. Day two is the big sightseeing day: the Giza Pyramids, the Great Sphinx and the Valley Temple, the Step Pyramid at Saqqara, and the Grand Egyptian Museum, with lunch included. On day three you explore the city's history: the treasures of the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir Square, the Citadel of Salah El Din with the Mosque of Muhammad Ali on its hilltop, and the lanes of Khan El Khalili, a bazaar that has been trading since the 14th century.

In Hurghada you stay at a 5-star resort by the sea. After you arrive on day four, the rest of the day is free to settle in and enjoy the beach. Day five is a snorkeling trip over the coral reefs of the Red Sea, with lunch included. Day six takes you into the desert behind the coast on a quad-bike safari, with a Bedouin-style atmosphere and dinner included. On day seven you fly back to Cairo for your international departure.

sections.h: When to Go and What It Costs
body: The package runs all year. The lowest prices are from May to September, when Cairo is hot but the Red Sea is at its warmest. October to April is the most comfortable time for sightseeing in Cairo, while the Christmas and New Year period is the busiest and most expensive. The price per person also depends on group size, from groups of 9 to 16 down to solo travelers; every combination is in the price table above.

sections.h: What Is Included and What to Plan
body: **Included:** six nights in 5-star hotels, domestic flights, private air-conditioned transport, an Egyptologist guide, entrance fees to all listed sights, the snorkeling trip and the quad-bike safari.
**Not included:** international flights, your Egypt entry visa, tips and personal expenses.
**Visa:** many nationalities can get a visa on arrival or apply online through Egypt's official e-visa portal. Check the rules for your passport before you travel.

**Changes:** ask us if you would like to swap an activity — for example the quad-bike safari for a [Luxor day trip from Hurghada](/tours/luxor-day-trip-from-hurghada/) or an [Orange Bay island trip](/tours/orange-bay-island-snorkeling/).

Prefer one night less in Hurghada? The [6-day Cairo and Hurghada package](/packages/6-days-cairo-hurghada-package/) keeps the same Cairo program. To add the temples of Upper Egypt, the [8-day Cairo, Abu Simbel, Luxor and Hurghada package](/packages/8-days-cairo-abu-simbel-luxor-hurghada/) includes Abu Simbel and Luxor. Our [Cairo travel guide](/blog/cairo-travel-guide-pyramids-museums-bazaars/) and [Hurghada vs Sharm El Sheikh guide](/blog/red-sea-egypt-resorts-hurghada-vs-sharm-guide/) help you plan the details.
